properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding expected.
Dangerous rip currents and elevated surf expected along west-
facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to noon PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the advisory area should prepare for rising
water and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Highest tides will occur in the late morning each day. Observed
high tides are 1.3 to 1.6 feet above astronomical tide
predictions. Surf will increase starting Monday, but there is
uncertainty in details at this time.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to rise in Action Stage. The river is forecast to climb into Minor
flood stage in the next couple days, with a continued rise through
Minor flood stage this weekend and early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.2 feet, Water completely surrounds many homes in the
Stone Island and Still Brook subdivisions. Pool enclosures and
patios become flooded. Water covers many of the roads. Flooding
occurs on Enterprise Road and in the Bethel Loop subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Saturday morning and continue rising to 6.2 feet Tuesday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS, ESPECIALLY LATE TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY...

.Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will be on the increase,
peaking on Saturday. During the peak, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will
be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties. Meanwhile, the air will warm and dry, with
minimum humidities in the 8 to 20 percent range common by
Saturday. Fuels remain critically dry despite some minor greenup
from recent rains. There is a high risk for fast-moving fires
where the plants are driest and the winds are strongest, which
this targeted Red Flag Warning addresses.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Western Santa Monica
Mountains Recreational Area, Eastern Santa Monica Mountains
Recreational Area, Santa Susana Mountains and Western San
Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor.

* TIMING...From 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph. Isolated
gusts 45 to 55 mph in most favored locations.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent. Poor overnight
recoveries.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 6 at 9:53AM PST until November 7 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 6 at 10:08AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 6 at 1:25AM EST until November 8 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; South Washington Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement on the beaches, sneaker
waves possible. For the High Surf Warning, large sneaker waves
and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 33 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop and Tillamook Coast, and South Washington
Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Warning, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 6 at 11:59PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 10 to 16 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 7.1 to 7.4 feet (MLLW) are
expected each morning.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one quarter foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between
8.8 and 9.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 9 AM to 11 AM PST
this morning. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday. High tide is at 9:51 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide with
high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This will
allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 2:44AM PST until November 7 at 11:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

north through the basin.

forecast.

forecast.

submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.3 feet.

flood stage at 3.3 feet late this week with a slow rise this
weekend reaching 3.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Cocoa to rise
into Moderate flood stage. The river is forecast to rise into Major
flood stage late this week and remain within Major Flood Stage this
weekend and into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 PM EST Thursday was 16.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, reaching
Major flood stage late this week. It is forecast to crest at 17.1
feet late this weekend into early next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.

* WHAT...Sneaker waves possible on the beaches.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Waves can run up significantly farther on a beach
than normal, including over rocks and jetties. Sneaker waves
can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull
them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or
drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.

properties.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS, ESPECIALLY LATE FRIDAY NIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY...

.Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will be on the increase,
peaking on Saturday. During the peak, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will
be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties. Meanwhile, the air will warm and dry, with
minimum humidities in the 8 to 20 percent range common by
Saturday. Fuels remain critically dry despite some minor greenup
from recent rains. There is a high risk for fast-moving fires
where the plants are driest and the winds are strongest, which
this targeted Red Flag Warning addresses.

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a
Red Flag Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in
effect from 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains
Recreational Area, Santa Susana Mountains and Western San
Gabriel Mountains.

* TIMING...From 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* WINDS...Periods of northeast 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 45 mph.
Isolated gusts of 45 to 55 mph possible.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent. Poor overnight
recoveries.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 5 at 1:36PM PST until November 7 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 2 AM TO 6 PM PST SATURDAY FOR WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR THE WESTERN SAN GABRIELS, THE SANTA SUSANAS, THE SANTA MONICAS, AND THE SANTA CLARITA VALLEY

properties.areaDesc: Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 9:08 AM
Friday 11/6, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 9:38 AM
Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06 AM
Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 5 at 11:25AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:06
AM Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 10:35 AM
Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:04 AM
Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 11:35 AM
Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 11:38AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to rise in Action Stage. The river is forecast to climb into Minor
flood stage in the next couple days, with a continued rise through
Minor flood stage through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.2 feet, Water completely surrounds many homes in the
Stone Island and Still Brook subdivisions. Pool enclosures and
patios become flooded. Water covers many of the roads. Flooding
occurs on Enterprise Road and in the Bethel Loop subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage over
the next couple of days and will continue rising to 6.3 feet
early next week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high
tide is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
9:38 AM Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
10:06 AM Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
10:35 AM Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
11:04 AM Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
11:35 AM Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.6 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 12 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday
November 13. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high
tide is expected to be: 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
9:38 AM Saturday 11/7, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
10:06 AM Sunday 11/8, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at
10:35 AM Monday 11/9, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at
11:04 AM Tuesday 11/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
11:35 AM Wednesday 11/11, 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 6 at 6:31PM PST until November 9 at 10:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream will maintain river levels
within Moderate flood stage through early next week as a large volume
of rainwater works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Saturday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24
feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between
8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM to noon PST
Sunday. High tide is at 10:21 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous surf
conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly
discouraged!

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide with
high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This will
allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 11:41AM PST until November 8 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY
NEW FIRE STARTS, ESPECIALLY LATE TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY...

.Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will be on the increase,
peaking on Saturday. During the peak, gusts of 30 to 45 mph will
be common in the typical wind-prone areas of Los Angeles and
Ventura Counties. Meanwhile, the air will warm and dry, with
minimum humidities in the 8 to 20 percent range common by
Saturday. Fuels remain critically dry despite some minor greenup
from recent rains. There is a high risk for fast-moving fires
where the plants are driest and the winds are strongest, which
this targeted Red Flag Warning addresses.

* AFFECTED AREA...Santa Clarita Valley, Western Santa Monica
Mountains Recreational Area, Eastern Santa Monica Mountains
Recreational Area, Santa Susana Mountains and Western San
Gabriel Mountains and Highway 14 Corridor.

* TIMING...From 2 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.
Isolated gusts 45 to 55 mph in most favored locations.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 20 percent. Poor
overnight recoveries.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 6 at 3:14PM PST until November 7 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until midnight PST
tonight. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach
erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged! Large, unexpected
waves can sweep across the beach without warning, sweeping
people into the sea from rocks, jetties, and beaches. These
sneaker waves can also move large objects such as logs,
crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 2:30PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement on the beaches, sneaker
waves possible. For the High Surf Advisory on the beaches, large
waves, hazardous surf conditions, and sneaker waves. Breakers
up to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and
other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline due
to sneaker waves. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which
may lead to serious injury or drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Caution should be used when in or near
the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 6 at 12:57PM PST until November 8 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.
